why: Isaiah 59:16 'And he saw' has no subject; 59:15 names the LORD as the one who saw

Jeremiah 11 ends mid-sentence on 11:21 'by our hand:'; ending on Jeremiah's plea in 11:20 is clean, and the slot restores Ebed-melech's approach to the king (38:8), without which 38:9 'My lord the king' has no speaker
Jeremiah 24 ends mid-sentence on 24:8 'in the land of Egypt:'; 25:10 repeats the bridegroom/bride refrain already kept twice
Jeremiah 26:6 'Then will I make this house like Shiloh' hangs without the condition in 26:4; 27:17 repeats 27:12 and 27:14
Ezekiel 28:2 'Because thine heart is lifted up...' never reaches its 'therefore'; 27:5 is inessential ship-building detail
Jeremiah 21:4 answers the king's envoys but nothing says Jeremiah is replying

bridges.Jeremiah 21:4: Jeremiah sends the envoys back to Zedekiah with God's answer.

why: Jeremiah 32:17 'Ah Lord GOD!' switches to Jeremiah praying without signal

bridges.Jeremiah 32:17: Once the deed is handed to Baruch, Jeremiah prays.

why: Jeremiah 39:4 'when Zedekiah saw them' points at the Babylonian princes of 39:3, who are never mentioned

bridges.Jeremiah 39:4: The Babylonian commanders march in and take their seats in the city's middle gate.

why: Jeremiah 39:14 'Even they sent' has no subject; the senders (39:13) are dropped

bridges.Jeremiah 39:14: Nebuzar-adan and the Babylonian officers carry out the king's order.

why: Jeremiah 40:14 begins mid-sentence 'And said unto him'; the bridge should end by bringing Johanan to Gedaliah

bridges.Jeremiah 40:14: Scattered Judean army captains rally to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Their leader, Johanan son of Kareah, comes to him with a warning.

why: Jeremiah 44:15 'the men which knew that their wives had burned incense' answers a rebuke the reader never heard

bridges.Jeremiah 44:15: Jeremiah warns the Jews in Egypt that by burning incense to other gods they are repeating the sin that destroyed Jerusalem.

why: Jeremiah 45:5 'And seekest thou great things' answers a complaint of Baruch's that is dropped

bridges.Jeremiah 45:5: Baruch has cried out that God has added grief to his sorrow. God answers that he is about to tear down the whole land he built.

why: Ezekiel 17:12 'what these things mean' follows only the first line of the riddle; the vine and second eagle that 17:13-15 interpret are missing

bridges.Ezekiel 17:12: The eagle plants a native seed that grows into a low vine, but the vine turns its roots toward a second great eagle.
